messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — escalation from customer acme-inc: since ~05:58 UTC many requests are being routed to us-east-1 instead of eu-west-1. Customers seeing 300–800ms cross-region latency and occasional 401s. Ticket #3421. Anyone on this?

devin_infra: looking now. which routing policy was deployed recently? :mag:

leo_network: i see routing-policy v3 deployed at 05:58:22 UTC. config shows RegionCacheTTL set to 86400 in the deployed env (should be 300). pushing logs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: routing-config v3 deployed to nexus at 05:58:22 UTC by jamie_prod.

sarah_sre: can you paste a failing req id + headers? need x-client-region/x-rw-selected-region from the response to confirm.

maria_support: sample from ticket: req_id=abcd1234, user=acme-alpha, ts=1764812530. headers:```x-client-region: eu-west-1
x-rw-routing: prefer-nearest
x-auth-token: <redacted>``` response had `x-rw-selected-region: us-east-1` and latency ~512ms. customer also saw intermittent 401s.

devin_infra: trace for abcd1234 shows router consulted policy store, matched policy, but region lookup returned stale mapping to us-east-1. Cache read returned TTL=86400s.

leo_network: confirmed. rollout accidentally changed default REGION_CACHE_TTL from 300 -> 86400 because `REGION_CACHE_TTL` env var was missing in the template and default fell back to msisd (bad). that explains persistent stale mapping.

jamie_prod: i initiated rollback to routing-config v2 at 06:10. then forced cache purge for affected routing nodes at 06:12. customer reports improved latency by 06:18.

maria_support: acme confirms latency normalized and 401s stopped after purge. no new errors in last 30m.

sarah_sre: preliminary root cause: misconfigured env var during routing-policy v3 rollout caused region cache TTL to be set to 24h; fallback behavior preferred the last-known region, so traffic for eu customers went to us-east-1. contributing factors: missing deploy-time validation for TTL; no synthetic alert for sudden cross-region traffic. drafting postmortem.

devin_infra: reproducible steps (staging):
1) set `REGION_CACHE_TTL=86400` in routing agent
2) deploy policy v3
3) send request with `x-client-region: eu-west-1` -> router returns `x-rw-selected-region: us-east-1` because cache entry persisted

curl example:
```bash
curl -H "x-client-region: eu-west-1" -H "x-auth-token: ..." -i https://api.redwood.ai/generate 
# check `x-rw-selected-region` in response headers
```

leo_network: mitigations executed: rollback to v2, `redwoodctl routing purge --region-cache` on affected nodes, and emergency hotfix to set default TTL=300 in agent binary.

jamie_prod: i added an emergency runbook entry and a manual alert to page oncall if >5% of requests cross-region in a 5m window. i'll open PR to require TTL env var and add deploy-time validation.

maria_support: i'll draft the customer-facing note and propose a 2-hour credit. need a concise timeline for them.

sarah_sre: timeline draft for comms:
- 05:58:22 UTC — routing-config v3 deployed (bad default TTL)
- ~06:01:30 UTC — first support report of elevated latency from acme
- 06:05:10 UTC — SRE began investigation (manual alerts + support)
- 06:10:05 UTC — rollback to routing-config v2 initiated
- 06:12:00 UTC — regional cache purge executed
- 06:18:40 UTC — acme confirms latency normalized
- 06:30:00 UTC — metrics back to baseline

devin_infra: proposed action items (owners):
- enforce non-zero TTL default and schema validation (PR #987) — devinfra
- add CI test to simulate cache TTL mismatch and ensure routing correctness — devinfra
- add synthetic checker for cross-region ratio >1% over 5m — obs team
- add alerting for correlated rise in 4xx/401s with region mismatch — sres

jamie_prod: taking PR #987 and runbook updates.

maria_support: i'll send draft to acme, cc legal for credit approval. thanks everyone.

ops-bot: incident-bot: Incident IN-2026-03-12-RR created. Severity: P2. Owner: sarah_sre.

sarah_sre: i'll publish full postmortem to /incident-postmortems/IN-2026-03-12-RR later today and add the timeline + action item owners. tagging @oncall for follow-ups. Thanks all.
